findings.trigger_condition: Input contains a mix of distinct hashable and unhashable nodes with no cross-equality (e.g., 5000 distinct hashable strings like 'h{i}' plus 5000 distinct unhashable lists like [f'u{i}'], each dependent on a common 'root'). Any workload where both hashable_ids and unhashable_ids grow to O(N) triggers the defect, even with fully distinct values.
findings.root_cause: In _id_of() the hashable path (lines 74-84) always scans the entire unhashable_ids list after checking hash_buckets, even when a bucket hit already found a match. The unhashable path (lines 58-72) symmetrically always scans hashable_ids after scanning unhashable_ids, even when the first scan found a match, to select the earliest first-appearance id. For distinct nodes the second scan never finds a match and must iterate the whole opposite registry (O(H) or O(U)) to confirm absence of cross-type equality. This makes every node registration O(N) and the whole graph O(N^2). The reference plan expects cross-check only on miss / short-circuit on hit; candidate-B does bidirectional unconditional scans.
findings.impact: O(N^2) time during node deduplication for mixed hashable/unhashable graphs. Empirically validated: mixed workload (N/2 hashable + N/2 unhashable, all distinct) takes ~0.12s at N=2000, ~0.73s at N=5000 (6.08x for 2.5x growth, ~quadratic), ~2.98s at N=10000 (4.1x for 2x growth, ~quadratic) and ~6.48s at N=15000, while pure-hashable deep chain of 20000 nodes takes only ~0.03s. The defect exhausts the 5s criterion timeout (res_dependency_20000 / supplemental wide_50000) on large mixed inputs and violates the implicit linearithmic performance contract, though pure-hashable probes still pass.
findings.suggested_validation: Load candidate-B and benchmark: def gen(): for i in range(N//2): yield (f'h{i}','root'); for i in range(N//2): yield ([f'u{i}'],'root'); time dependency_layers(gen()) for N=2000,5000,10000 and observe ~6x and ~4x scaling (quadratic) vs. linear. Contrast with pure hashable chain (i,i-1) for i in 1..20000 which stays <0.04s. Also verify the unconditional scan: instrument _id_of to count iterations of the second loop — it runs even when the first loop already matched, e.g., cross_hashability test with HashableNode('same') then UnhashableNode('same') still scans hashable_ids despite already finding the equal in unhashable_ids.
